prompt:
full-body portrait card, character centered, dramatic cool rim light from the side, soft even lighting. subject: Protée, the old shapeshifting sea god of Greek myth, a stocky old man with a long flowing beard made of seaweed and sea foam, a crown of coral and shells, deep Aegean blue skin with sea-green scales creeping over his shoulders, wearing a draped chiton of fishing net and kelp, caught mid-transformation with one arm becoming a curling octopus tentacle and his lower body turning into a swirl of water with fish tails, a sly knowing wink and a crooked grin, holding a trident-shaped driftwood staff, (scenery:-3) (cast shadow:-2), isolated on a flat plain white background.

Style: a painterly young-adult fantasy novel cover illustration with clean confident linework, soft cel shading with rich painted light, appealing slightly stylised proportions and expressive faces, in a sun-bleached Mediterranean palette of marble white, warm terracotta, olive green and deep Aegean blue with small burnished gold accents; dramatic but never gory or horrific, adventurous and a little theatrical, the feel of a Greek-mythology adventure book for teenagers.
